record.original_question: Which compact symmetric spaces of group type, without assuming simple connectivity, admit manifold quotients that are isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 7.6. Which compact symmetric spaces of group type (not necessarily simply connected) cover isospectral manifolds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact Riemannian symmetric space is said to be of group type if it is isometric to a compact connected Lie group G equipped with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric (so the isometric symmetric space structure is given by left and right translations). Two closed Riemannian manifolds are called isospectral if the eigenvalues of their Laplace–Beltrami operators, counted with multiplicities, coincide; they are isometric if there is a Riemannian isometry between them.

Say that a compact Riemannian manifold (M, g) "covers isospectral manifolds" if there exist two closed Riemannian manifolds M_1 and M_2, each obtained as a quotient of M by a discrete group of isometries acting freely and properly discontinuously, such that M_1 and M_2 are isospectral but not isometric.

Problem. Determine, without any assumption of simple connectivity, exactly which compact symmetric spaces of group type (G, g_0) — where G is a compact connected Lie group and g_0 is a bi-invariant metric — cover a pair of closed manifolds that are isospectral but not isometric.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem regarding the classification of group-type compact symmetric spaces (dropping simple connectivity) whose quotients yield isospectral but non-isometric manifolds. While Sunada-type constructions and results showing irreducible group-type symmetric spaces cover isospectral non-isometric manifolds are known, a complete classification in the non-simply-connected setting does not appear in the literature, and no resolution of this specific classification question was found.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral and isoscattering manifolds: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of techniques (Sunada method, torus method) producing isospectral non-isometric quotients of symmetric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Many constructions are known, but a complete classification for compact group-type symmetric spaces without simple connectivity is not stated.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2305.10950v2
status_evidence.snippet: Question 7.6 asks which compact symmetric spaces of group type (not necessarily simply connected) cover isospectral manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as open.
